VibeUsage API Docs for AI Token Usage Tracking
The VibeUsage API exposes scoped InsForge Edge Function endpoints for CLI ingestion, usage monitoring, model analytics, project summaries, public sharing, and leaderboard reads.
Read user analytics with usage:read endpoints such as /functions/vibeusage-usage-summary, /functions/vibeusage-usage-daily, and /functions/vibeusage-usage-model-breakdown.
Upload CLI usage with a device token through /functions/vibeusage-ingest and record sync health through /functions/vibeusage-sync-ping.
Read public leaderboard data anonymously or with a user JWT through /functions/vibeusage-leaderboard and /functions/vibeusage-leaderboard-profile.
Use the OpenAPI document for request schemas, response schemas, security schemes, and required permissions.
VibeUsage Auth Docs - Scoped Permissions for AI Agents
VibeUsage authentication docs covering scoped user JWTs, device tokens, share tokens, service role credentials, and agent permission boundaries.
VibeUsage Auth Docs and Scoped Permissions
VibeUsage separates access by credential role so agents can request the least powerful token needed for the task.
User JWTs read the signed-in user's analytics, issue device tokens, manage public visibility, and read optional self-aware leaderboard context.
Device tokens are limited to usage ingestion and sync heartbeat writes; they cannot read dashboards, public profiles, or admin endpoints.
Share tokens are limited to privacy-safe public profile and shared dashboard reads.
Service role keys are admin credentials for maintenance jobs and must never be exposed to browser clients or general-purpose agents.
Webhook status for VibeUsage developer integrations and agent-readiness discovery.
VibeUsage does not currently expose outbound webhooks; integrations should use scoped read endpoints, sync heartbeat state, and the MCP/OpenAPI resources listed here.
For current usage state, call user-scoped usage analytics endpoints with usage:read.
For sync freshness, use the sync fields returned by hourly usage and the device heartbeat endpoint.
For future webhook requests, open a GitHub issue with the event type, delivery target, and replay requirements.
Agents should treat this page as the canonical webhook capability statement until a webhook API appears in OpenAPI.
VibeUsage MCP Server and Manifest for AI Agents
VibeUsage MCP discovery resources for AI agents, including manifest JSON, OpenAPI links, and supported tool intents.
VibeUsage publishes a valid MCP manifest for agent discovery and maps common agent tools to OpenAPI operations for usage summaries, model breakdowns, and public leaderboard reads.
The MCP manifest is available at /.well-known/mcp/manifest.json and declares Streamable HTTP transport metadata for agent scanners.
The manifest points agents to /openapi.json so they can inspect request schemas and scoped permissions automatically.
Initial tool intents cover usage summary reads, model breakdown reads, and public leaderboard reads.
Agents that need write access should prefer scoped device-token ingestion rather than user or service-role credentials.

Install with npx --yes vibeusage init and complete the browser link flow to create a scoped device token.
